caption: The Blackcastle, our 16th-century Norman tower house keeping watch over the western end of the village. The lovely red-trim cottage out front gives a great sense of just how big the keep really is, and on a sunny day with the trees in leaf this is one of the best views in TMB

A closer look at the keep itself. You can see all four storeys of the Norman tower house, the corner turret, and the gorgeous medieval stonework that has been standing on the western edge of the village for the better part of five hundred years.

The Blackcastle seen from the back across an unmown meadow, framed by Hawthorn in full May blossom. Hawthorn is the traditional Irish 'May tree' and a foundational native species in our biodiversity plan, supporting hundreds of insect, bird and small mammal species across its life cycle. Five hundred years of Norman stonework, a season of native white blossom, and a meadow full of pollinator habitat all in a single frame (May 2026)
